はい、と時代がかったランプを手渡された。

“Then, to begin with, try using Reinforcement on this lamp.

“All you need to do is increase the strength of the glass around it.”

With that, she hands me an old-fashioned lamp.

pages.en:
“—”

I sit down on the floor.

Holding the lamp in both hands, I draw a long, deep breath.

Tohsaka makes it sound simple, but my whole body is rigid with tension.

pages.ja:
毎晩やっている事とはいえ、成功率は実にれーてんいちパーセントを切っているのが現状なのである。
遠坂は俺の腕前を計るために“強化”の度合いを見るというが、そもそも強化が成功しなかったら腕前を計るも何もない。

pages.en:
I may do this every night, but at present my success rate is less than 0.1 percent.

Tohsaka says she will judge my skill by the degree of Reinforcement. But if the Reinforcement itself fails, there will be no skill for her to judge.

“—”

No. I drive the distractions from my mind.

First, I focus my awareness on the lamp.

浮かび上がってくるのはランプの設計図だ。
ガラスの材質とカタチ、力の流れ、人間でいうところの血管まで図面にできる。
なら、あとはその血管に自身の魔力を注ぎ込むだけだ。

pages.en:
A blueprint of the lamp rises into view.

I can map the material and shape of the glass, the flow of force through it—even what would be blood vessels in a human body.

All that remains is to pour my own magical energy into those vessels.

決して人の体とは相容れない、焼けた神経を一本だけ体に突き刺し、自分の体になじませるだけ。

…I only have to proceed as I always do.

The sensation of driving a red-hot iron rod into my spine.

Take one burning nerve, something utterly incompatible with the human body, stab it into myself, and force my body to accept it.

If that goes well, all I need do is feed the glass precisely as much magical energy as it can bear—

pages.en:
“—Ah.”

I broke it.

I must have lost control. I pour in more magical energy than the proper amount, and the glass shatters without resistance.

“Hm? What did you suspect, Tohsaka?”

“Isn't it obvious? I'm appalled by your complete lack of talent…! You haven't even mastered the fundamentals. Frankly, I'm amazed you can generate magical energy at all with such a preposterous method!”

pages.ja: 「……遠坂。その、もしかして怒ってる？」
pages.jaRuby: 「……遠坂。その、もしかして怒ってる？」
pages.en: “…Tohsaka. Are you angry, by any chance?”

pages.ja:
「当たり前じゃない！ こんな基本的な問題を抱えたまま鍛錬してきたアンタにも呆れてるし、間違いをたださなかったアンタの師には殺意さえ覚えるわ。
なんだってアンタは、こんな遠回りなコトになってるのよ……！」

pages.en:
“Of course I am! I'm appalled that you kept training with such a fundamental problem, and I could almost murder the teacher who never corrected it.

“How did you end up taking such an absurdly circuitous path…!?”

pages.ja: 「……む。言っているコトは判らないが、親父の悪口はよせ。俺に才能がないのは俺の責任なんだから、親父は関係ないだろ」

pages.en: “…Hmph. I don't understand what you're talking about, but don't insult my father. My lack of talent is my own fault. It has nothing to do with him.”

pages.en:
“It has everything to do with him. Once you take someone on as a student, it is a teacher's duty to set them on the proper path.

“…I know there is no point taking my anger out on someone who is gone. Even so, your teacher got the very first step wrong.”

pages.ja:

その、外国の子供が愛用していそうな、色とりどりのドロップが入った缶だ。
日本でも類似品をよく見かける。
何種類かのあめ玉が入っていて、白色をしたドロップはハッカ味っていうアレだ。

pages.en:
Still fuming, Tohsaka takes something like a tin from her luggage.

It is the sort of tin a child overseas might treasure, filled with brightly colored drops. You often see similar ones in Japan: several flavors of hard candy, with the white drops tasting of peppermint.

pages.ja:
「士郎、手、出して」
「？」
とりあえず手を出す。
遠坂は缶をふって、赤っぽいドロップを出した。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Shirou. Hold out your hand.”

“?”

For the moment, I obey.

Tohsaka shakes the tin and tips a reddish drop into my palm.

「？？？」
とりあえず、言われた通りに口に運ぶ。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Here. Swallow that.”

“???”

For the moment, I do as she says and put it in my mouth.

いや、むしろ味なんてない。
それにこの舌触り、飴っていうより石なんじゃないだろうか。

pages.en:
“…It isn't sweet.”

In fact, it has no taste at all.

And judging by the feel of it against my tongue, this is closer to a stone than a piece of candy.

pages.en:
“…Ngh…”

I force it down with a gulp.

“Ow! My esophagus is burning. What did you just make me swallow, Tohsaka?”

Without so much as blinking, Tohsaka says something outrageous.

pages.ja:

「仕方ないでしょ。薬も用意してきたんだけど、士郎を矯正するにはそんな物じゃ効かないの。だから一番強いのでスイッチを開くしかないなって」

pages.en:
“A gem!? Why would you—!?”

“I had no choice. I brought medicine too, but something that mild would never correct your problem. So I decided I would have to force your switch open with the strongest thing I had.”

pages.ja: 「いや、そういうコトじゃなくてだな……！ なんだって宝石なんか飲ますんだよ、おまえは！ そんなん消化できるか！」

今のは、まだ判ってない貴方に、無理矢理判らせる為の強制装置。そろそろ溶け始める頃だから、気合い入れてないと気絶するわよ」

“…Listen. If you insist on worrying, at least worry about the right thing. That was no ordinary gem.

“What you swallowed is a forcing device, meant to make someone who still doesn't understand comprehend it by force. It should begin dissolving soon, so brace yourself unless you want to lose consciousness.”

」

“What do you mean, 'lose consciousness'!? You can't say something so dangerous with that cheerful—”

Before I can finish, the abnormality arrives.

意識を眉間に集めて、ぎゅっと絞っていなければ立っていられない。

pages.en:
“—!?”

My body is burning.

All sensation deserts my arms and legs.

Heat that can only be called pain gathers in my back.

Unless I gather my awareness between my brows and hold it there with all my strength, I cannot remain standing.

“—You… This is…”

I know this.

I know this feeling.

This is failure.

This is the rejection that tears through my body whenever I fail to build Magic Circuits into myself—!

pages.en:
“You'll be all right. It will be painful, but if you maintain your present condition, it should gradually become easier. The heat in your body will probably last two or three weeks, though.”

…I would like to say something in reply, but I have no strength to spare.

Right now, every part of me is occupied with the simple task of keeping my body upright.

“Listen. The difference between a mage and an ordinary human is whether or not they possess a switch.

“You understand that the switch turns the Magic Circuits on and off, don't you? Look at that electric kettle. It can boil water. A mage is like that. An ordinary person is like a thermos: it cannot boil water, but it can keep water hot.”

お湯を沸かすスイッチの有る無しは、もう個人ではどうしようもない問題でしょ。

pages.en:
“We may seem similar, but we are different things.

“Whether the switch for boiling water exists is beyond any individual's control. At birth—no, at the moment we are made—we are divided into electric kettles and thermoses. Anyone without that switch will pass their entire life without experiencing magecraft.”

つまり適性はあるのよ。だから一度でも魔術回路を体内に作ってしまえば、あとは切り替えるだけでいい。

“Listen carefully. You may be a novice, but you unquestionably possess Magic Circuits. In other words, you have the aptitude.

“Once you have created Magic Circuits inside your body, all you need do thereafter is switch them. Press the button, turn yourself on or off, and the magical energy will come.”

pages.en:
…I steady my breathing.

Tohsaka appears to be right. So long as I keep myself under control, my condition does not grow any worse.

pages.en: “A mage needs to create their Magic Circuits only once. But every time you practice, you begin from nothing, create the circuits anew, and try to build them into yourself.”

It is a merciless judgment, perfectly characteristic of Tohsaka.

I mutter my complaint at the man who is no longer there.
